burst-star.png.notes: TIER A. Crop 1152x1152 centred, reduce 16x to 72x72. ONE image emits 15 sprites: 3 tints (Bone #E9E4D8 / Amber #FFB454 / Klaxon #FF4A36) x 5 fade stages via dimmed(), with the pedestal-mine burst scaled to 48x48. Fires on Part 7's pivotal beats: death peak-white, mine ignition (1-frame white + red cross-flash), Fortress ignition starburst. THE ALPHA DISCIPLINE MATTERS MOST HERE (risk #2): dimmed() scales alpha proportionally, so any residual haze in the empty corners survives every fade stage as a dim floating rectangle over the board — the one failure dimmed() cannot rescue. Baker: a < 24 -> bitwise (0,0,0,0), then assert the alpha histogram has zero mass in 1..23 and the transparent region is exactly zero. The speck floor (1/36 of the diameter) is the reduction arithmetic made explicit: 1152/36 = 32 source px = 2 px at 72, which is the smallest speck that survives a 16x area reduction with alpha above the 24 cutoff. WARNING: FadeStages cannot be raised without re-spacing sprite ids 920/924/928/932 — they are packed exactly FadeStages apart and will silently overlap.
burst-star.png.prompt:
Orthographic front view, straight on, no perspective, no camera tilt.
Single key light from the upper left. No cast shadow (the shadow is drawn separately).
Background: flat pure #00FF00, edge to edge. There must be no other green anywhere.
No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature.

A single radial burst seen flat on, centred on flat pure #00FF00. Draw it as a flat monochrome mask in one solid near-black blue #10161C, with no shading, no gradient, no colour variation and no soft edge anywhere — only its silhouette survives, and the renderer tints and fades it.

Eight straight tapering rays radiate from a small solid core: one up, one down, one left, one right and one along each diagonal, each ray widest where it meets the core and narrowing to a blunt tip, all eight the same length and thickness, so the figure is symmetric about both axes and both diagonals. The core is a solid disc about one sixth of the star's diameter.

Between the rays, a scatter of small separate specks — hard-edged squares and stubby wedges, not dots of light — dense near the core and thinning outward, so the outer part of the figure breaks into particles instead of ending cleanly. The scatter is irregular; the rays are not.

No smoke, no fire, no flame, no embers with trails, no lens flare, no glow, no bloom, no halo, no motion blur, no soft falloff, no vignette: every edge is a hard cut and nothing is drawn at partial opacity.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 72x72 pixel sprite and again to 48x48: no ray narrower than one twentieth of the star's diameter at its base, and no separate speck smaller than one thirty-sixth of the star's diameter.

Draw it centred, spanning a little more than half the frame's width, with a wide clean flat key-colour margin all the way around.

The subject will be composited onto a dark slate ground, RGB(40,48,57) — light it for that.

Palette, strictly:
  structure / stone / chassis  -> desaturated blue-grey, #1C242B to #4E5E6B only
  living signal / emission     -> pale cyan phosphor #A5E3EE, highlights to #EAF7FA
  matter, loot, money, energy  -> warm amber #FFB454
  contact shadow / ink line    -> near-black blue #10161C
Nothing warm except the amber. Nothing green. Nothing saturated red unless asked.

bush-clump.png.notes: TIER A. Crop 1536x1536, reduce 64x to 24x24. ONE image emits four sprites (SpBushBase 90..93): code composites 0-3 amber pips on top at fixed spots. Note the deliberate contrast with the rock entries: rocks MUST fill their footprint opaquely because tkRock is a collider; bushes MUST NOT, because a bush is an entity on LayerMap with charges, blocks nothing, and reads better with floor visible around it. Phase 0 prerequisite: SpBushBase 90..93 currently collides with SpProjBase + ord(iArrows|iDarts) = 91,92 in the same spriteDefs packet — last define wins, so two of the three bush charge states render as an 8x8 projectile blob today. Move SpProjBase to 960 before this art means anything.

floor-field-01.png.notes: TIER B. Four independent draws of ONE prompt, assembled by the baker into a 2x2 mosaic: -01 top-left, -02 top-right, -03 bottom-left, -04 bottom-right. Crop 2304x2304 from each — an INTERIOR window, never touching the frame edge, which is where the model puts its vignette — reduce 4x (two box-halvings) to 576x576, assemble to 1152x1152 = WorldPxR at RS=4. QUANTIZE ONCE, AFTER ASSEMBLY: four independently median-cut quadrants carry four palettes and the joins appear as colour steps across the middle of the board. Equalize per-quadrant mean and stddev BEFORE quantization if the joins fail. Verification, both mechanical: (a) block flatness — split the assembled 1152x1152 into an 8x8 grid of 144px blocks, assert every block's mean luma is within +/-3 of the field mean (kills vignettes, which are what make a mosaic seam findable); (b) join test — mean |dLuma| across the x=576 column join and the y=576 row join must not exceed 1.25x the mean |dLuma| of interior columns/rows. Consumed by plateAt as `base` in place of BgDark; plateAt keeps its per-tile shade hash, its PanelPeriodPx joints, its flecks and pinholes, and gains the two §3.4 deltas missing today (+3% luminance inside the safe ring; amber-etched Fortress chamber floor). Sample point is the ABSOLUTE world pixel (wx,wy) — this is why the field is full-arena and non-tiling: no two of the 2,040 ground tiles may match.

Consumed ONLY by parapetColorAt's `else: base` branch: the 4-ray openDistDir edge classification stays verbatim, StoneInk contact line at edge<=1, lit/shadowed bevel to WallBevelPx=8, roof seam at (wx+wy) mod RoofSeamPeriod. Fortress reuses the SAME material at shade(+22) — a brighter ramp, not a second image (§3.4). SEAMLESSNESS IS THE BAKER'S JOB, NOT THE MODEL'S: no supported frame size is a 2^k multiple of 384 (1024/384=2.67, 2048/384=5.33, 4096/384=10.67), so the crop is always an interior window and whatever tileability the model produced is cut away. Baker: (1) measure — edgeDelta = mean|L(x=383,y) - L(x=0,y)| over y, and the same for the y axis; interiorDelta = mean|L(x,y) - L(x+1,y)| over the interior; require edgeDelta <= 1.25 * interiorDelta on both axes; (2) if it fails, apply a deterministic wrap-blend over a 32px band (1/12 of the tile) with a cosine window, then re-measure; (3) block flatness — 8x8 grid of 48px blocks, each mean luma within +/-3 of the image mean, which is what keeps the 16-tile repeat undetectable. Order matters: wrap-blend BEFORE median-cut, or the blend invents off-ramp colours that the palette lint then rejects.
